question: Which of the following about phenytoin is true ?

options.opc: It is excreted unchanged in urine

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Phenytoin" -> "metabolized at a constant rate" -> "rate of elimination is independent of its concentration" -> "follows zero order kinetics" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin" -> "induces hepatic enzymes" -> "increases metabolism of other drugs" -> "is an hepatic enzyme inducer" -> 5%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin" -> "metabolized in the liver" -> "converted to inactive metabolites" -> "not excreted unchanged in urine" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Phenytoin" -> "associated with fetal hydantoin syndrome" -> "causes birth defects" -> "is teratogenic" -> 95%
analysis: Phenytoin is known to follow zero-order kinetics, meaning that it is metabolized at a constant rate regardless of its concentration in the blood. This is a well-established pharmacokinetic property of phenytoin. The other options are incorrect as phenytoin is a known hepatic enzyme inducer, it is not excreted unchanged in the urine (it undergoes hepatic metabolism), and it is teratogenic, associated with fetal hydantoin syndrome when used during pregnancy.
